payload.headline: 7-day activation fell from 40.1% to 36.9% for cohorts that signed up after Feb 10

cause.does_not_prove: Why Microsoft calendar users stopped activating.
cause.text: The drop is concentrated in Microsoft calendar workspaces: 39.4% before, 29.8% after.

cause.does_not_prove: That the release caused the drop.
cause.text: The onset matches rel_0412, Onboarding v2: connect calendar first, released Feb 10.

cause.does_not_prove: How many blocked users never wrote in.

evidence.quote: It says I need admin approval.

cause.text: Tickets about needing admin approval on the calendar step started in week 6, from 3 or more workspaces a week.

cause.does_not_prove: How many blocked workspaces would activate if given a fallback.

evidence.ref: first_meeting_rate_7d for microsoft, same periods: 0.5248 to 0.4392
exploratory: calendar_connect_failed with error_code admin_consent_required, by week

cause.text: Mechanism: v2 removed the skip, so orgs that require admin consent cannot reach a first meeting.

payload.cheapest_test: Roll back v2 for Microsoft calendar workspaces. Read first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d after 7 days.
payload.question: Why did activation fall, and what should we do about it?
payload.recommendation: Restore the skip for Microsoft calendar workspaces now. Retest v2 behind a flag, with a fallback when admin consent is required.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: That no Teams bot issue exists.

evidence.ref: exploratory: activation by calendar_provider and primary meeting_platform

ruled_out.text: The Teams bot is not the cause. Within Microsoft calendar workspaces, the drop is similar whether meetings run on Zoom or Teams.

size.method: bet.expected_value: 3.2-point activation gap x 23-point conversion gap between activated and not x 3,944 trials a week x $877 ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Share of blocked orgs whose admin approves within 7 days
would_change_if: Google calendar workspaces also dropped after Feb 10
Microsoft activation was already falling before Feb 10

payload.hypothesis: Restoring the skip for Microsoft calendar workspaces brings their activation back to baseline.
payload.kill_trigger: Microsoft first_meeting_rate_7d not back to its week 1 to 5 level for cohorts starting after the rollback

payload.does_not_prove: That v2 with a consent fallback would do better than v1.
payload.method: Mature cohorts from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-08 (1,433 workspaces) against 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-22

payload.rationale: The rollback recovered Microsoft activation to 38.2%, inside the predicted range. Next: retest v2 behind a flag with a consent fallback.
